conviction_note: Q3 is new (not pre-released) and the US counterparties who reported 22-28 Oct (Pool Corp sell-through +4% with inventory -3%, Hayward North America +9% with balanced channel inventory and 2027 early-buy orders ahead, Pentair Pool -18% on a destock it says is now complete) argue for a decent North American quarter. FX also turns from headwind to slight tailwind (EUR/USD Q3 avg 1.1506 vs 1.1689). Against that: all of this is proxy evidence that the market saw before the window opened (FDR +2.8% on 27 Oct, +1.1% intraday on 28 Oct), Europe is about half of sales and has no clean read, and the margin guide was already steered to the low-to-mid end. So p_up is only 57 on an abs_move of 6.0, giving (2*0.57-1)*6.0 = +0.84 against a findings sum of +1.2; the gap is the proxy discount and is deliberate.

findings.finding: Fluidra's US counterparties and peers reported 22-28 Oct with a healthy channel. Pool Corp (Fluidra's largest US distributor) had sales +4%, accelerating from +2% in Q2, with inventory -3%. Hayward's North America sales rose 9%, it cited 'balanced channel inventories' and 2027 early-buy orders ahead of last year, and it raised its FY guide. Pentair Pool fell 18% but said the channel inventory realignment is complete. Together this points to Fluidra's North American Q3 holding or beating H1's +4% and to positive early-buy commentary, which contradicts the Barclays May thesis of a US like-for-like decline over 2-3 quarters.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 prints moved FDR.MC +7.11% (31 Oct 2024) and +9.44% (30 Oct 2025), both on in-line-to-good quarters with the guide confirmed; the H1 2025 print fell 6.47% on a US/FX-driven miss.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced. The US peers rose +14.4% (POOL, 22 Oct), +12.8% (PNR, 27 Oct) and +11.6% (HAYW, 28 Oct intraday) on their prints, while FDR.MC gained only about +4% over the same days (+2.82% on 27 Oct, +1.13% on 28 Oct at the seal). If the read-across were fully in the price, FDR would have tracked its peers more closely; part of the gap is rational, since Fluidra is about half Europe and Hayward's E&RW fell 6%. Only Fluidra's own North America number settles it, and that is in the release.
findings.independence: Pool Corp Q3 release, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000945841/000119312526428428/pool-ex99_1.htm (2026-10-22); Pentair Q3 release, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000077360/000007736026000055/q32026pressrelease.htm (2026-10-27). Three separate documents, merged into one finding because they make one claim.

findings.finding: FX turns from headwind to slight tailwind in Q3. Average EUR/USD was 1.1506 in Q3 2026 against 1.1689 in Q3 2025 (USD about +1.6% y/y), after an FX drag of -5% in Q1 and -2% in H1, so reported sales and EBITDA growth should close the gap to constant-FX growth for the first time this year.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: FX was blamed for the Q1 2026 profit decline (stock +0.9% on 6 May 2026) and the H1 2025 miss (-6.47%); there is no clean case of an FX tailwind surprising.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: analysts model FX mechanically. What is left is the reported-number headline in Spanish wires ('crece X%' reported vs CFX), which in Q1 read as a profit decline. Small.
findings.independence: Renta 4 on the FX path in H1 (-5% Q1, -2% H1): https://www.r4.com/articulos-y-analisis/valores/fluidra-2t26-espanta-los-temores-en-el-sector

findings.finding: Possible further IEEPA tariff refunds inside Q3 adj. EBITDA. Fluidra booked about EUR5m in Q2, management pointed to refunds as upside to the low-to-mid-end margin guide, and Pentair booked about $8m of IEEPA refunds in its Q3. This is a one-off.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 included about EUR5m of refunds in an adj. EBITDA beat; the stock rose 2.04% then gave back 1.23% the next day.
findings.original_quote: Ajustando el EBITDA por los aproximadamente 5 mln eur de devolución de aranceles, el margen se situaría en 27,7% aproximadamente 50 pbs por encima de las previsiones.
findings.why_not_priced: Whether Q3 carries more refunds is not public. But analysts strip it out, and a beat made of a refund tends to be looked through, so it is worth very little.
findings.independence: Pentair Q3 2026 release, ~$8m IEEPA refunds in the quarter: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000077360/000007736026000055/q32026pressrelease.htm

findings.finding: The Middle East is a drag on Rest of World. Hayward's Europe & Rest of World sales fell 6% in Q3 'primarily due to lower volume resulting from geopolitical conflicts in the Middle East'. Fluidra said on its Q1 call that the region is about 3% of group sales and that it expected reduced activity there.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior print where the Middle East was the swing line.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced, because the company flagged it in May. The residual is the size of the Q3 hit on a 3% region, which nets out at tens of basis points of group growth.

baseline_tension: Agrees with the lean and the run-up: FDR is +4.07% over 5d and +5.49% over 20d, driven by the same peer prints, so the main finding largely restates what the free control already carries; the 60-day run-up (-7.95%) and the stock's lag against its US peers are the only orthogonal parts.
